thread:
erin.h: CSM forwarded a customer escalation — Dedicated pool eu-west-1 dropping throughput by ~50% since 09:10 UTC. APIs return higher latency and occasional 429s. Customer says it started after a model swap earlier this morning.
priya.s: Thanks Erin. Do we have pool id / tenant id? Any autoscale events in that window? @jason.m can you grab metrics? :eyes:
jason.m: Pool: dp-9843, tenant: acme-inc. I pulled a quick panel — tokens/s dropped from ~120k to ~60k at 09:08. Queue depth spiked then batches got much smaller. Looks like average batch tokens fell from ~3200 to ~700.
mark.k: That screams inefficient batching + max_batch_tokens interaction. Which model variant did they swap to?
erin.h: They switched from rwd-3-large to rwd-3-opt-quant at 09:05 (support ticket). CSM attached a short trace showing longer prefill times.
jason.m: Confirmed. prefill p99 increased from 40ms -> 220ms, decode still OK. Continuous-batcher kept waiting and produced thin microbatches. Autoscaler didn't kick because CPU/gpu utilization stayed below threshold (prefill is CPU-bound on host, but we use GPU util for autoscale).
priya.s: So autoscale policy watching GPU util missed bottleneck due to CPU prefill slowing batch formation. Could be noisy neighbor spiking CPU or a model change increasing tokenization/CPU work.
mark.k: Also check max_batch_tokens config — if smaller after model swap we might create more batches per request, increasing overhead. What's config for dp-9843?
jason.m: dp-9843 config snapshot: ``max_batch_tokens: 4096
max_wait_ms: 15
continuous_batching: enabled
prefill_cpu_pin: shared``
mark.k: Huh. Model swap to quantized variant added a heavier CPU tokenization path, continuous batching with low max_wait_ms produced many thin batches. That explains throughput drop and 429s as queue backs up.
nora.r: I can repro locally on a dev node — running the quantized model with a steady 40rps of 400-token requests drops average batch tokens rapidly. I'll post a small repro script.
infra-bot: @eng-runtime detected: pool dp-9843 high queue-depth event at 2026-03-17T09:10:08Z, queue_depth: 312, avg_batch_tokens: 682.
support-bot: Ticket #24587 updated: customer seeing 429/timeouts, CSM notified.
priya.s: Mitigation plan — short term: 1) increase max_wait_ms to 50 for dp-9843 to allow larger microbatches, or temporarily disable continuous_batching for that pool; 2) add CPU-based autoscale metric or set autoscale override to consider queue_depth; 3) route traffic to fallback model (rwd-3-large) until we stabilize. Which is quickest?
jason.m: Quickest is changing max_wait_ms on pool to 50 and set a temporary autoscale override to +1 replica. I can push the pool config and bump reserved capacity for them if needed.
mark.k: Also create a short-term throttle on noisy tenant(s) if we find any causing CPU spikes. But first confirm there's no infra regression.
erin.h: CSM asked for repro steps we can share. Nora — can you attach the load generator command?
nora.r: Repro command: ``./tools/loadgen --host https://inference.redwood.internal --pool dp-9843 --rps 40 --payload '{"prompt":"lorem ipsum","max_tokens":400}' --duration 5m``

nora.r: Observed metrics during repro: avg_batch_size: 4 reqs, avg_batch_tokens: 720, prefill_p95: 210ms, gpu_util: 28%, queue_depth: 200 -> 320. When I toggled continuous_batching off, avg_batch_tokens jumped to 2600 and tokens/s recovered to ~115k.
priya.s: Good repro. Action items: 1) Jason — bump max_wait_ms and scale +1 replica now, 2) Mark — run tenant sibling check to identify noisy neighbor processes on same host(s), 3) Nora — attach your perf snapshots to ticket, 4) Erin — inform CSM with ETA and mitigation.
jason.m: On it. Pushing config now: ``PATCH /admin/pools/dp-9843/config {"max_wait_ms":50}". Also applying autoscale override +1 replica.
infra-bot: Config change applied to dp-9843 by jason.m at 2026-03-17T09:22:03Z.
jason.m: Early telemetry after change: avg_batch_tokens climbed to ~2400, tokens/s rising back toward baseline, queue depth falling. Latency 95pct improving.
erin.h: I'll update support ticket and ping CSM. CSM wants a postmortem if this recurs.
mark.k: I'll run sibling tenant scan and look for CPU hogs or background jobs (model warmups, evals) that may have been colocated. If we find a noisy neighbor we'll isolate.
priya.s: Follow-up: longer term we should add a queue-depth-based autoscale signal and consider separate CPU metrics for prefill. Also add a canary step when swapping model variants that verifies prefill p95 on a staging host.
erin.h: Customer update posted: short-term fix applied, throughput recovering, working with eng to validate. CSM will monitor. :white_check_mark:
support-bot: Ticket #24587 comment: mitigation applied, customer notified.
mark.k: assigning a follow-up card for policy changes and a runbook note for "model swap -> perf smoke on dedicated pools".
priya.s: Thanks everyone. Keep this thread updated if anything regresses.
notes: thread focused on dedicated pool dp-9843 throughput regression after model swap; root cause: CPU-bound prefill + continuous-batching producing small batches; mitigation: increase max_wait_ms, autoscale override, route to fallback model; follow-ups: queue-depth autoscale signal, prefill canary for model swaps
